input.reasoning:
Estimate derived from 8 backlog items totalling 81 story points, converted to effort using a baseline of ~6-8 hours/point blended across roles depending on task type (infra, frontend UI, backend/API, integration, data migration). Role mix per task was assigned based on task nature (e.g. CI/staging -> DevOps+Backend; component library -> Frontend heavy; auth/RBAC/payments -> Backend heavy with QA; dashboard/invoice UI -> Frontend+Backend; data migration -> Backend+DevOps+QA). QA allocated ~15-20% of build hours per feature task for test design/execution. DevOps concentrated on pipeline and migration cutover support, respecting its low 0.4 FTE capacity (i.e. ~16 hrs/week for a project of this length). Backend Developer (1.5 FTE, ~60 hrs/week capacity) absorbs the largest share since most tasks (auth, RBAC, dashboard API, invoices API, Stripe integration, migration) are backend-centric. Frontend Developer (1.0 FTE, ~40 hrs/week) covers component library, dashboard UI, invoice UI, and UI portions of auth/RBAC. No historical actuals exist for this team, so effort figures are analogy/expert-judgement based with wide uncertainty bands reflected in the scenario percentiles. A 15% integration/PM contingency and a non-labour allowance for cloud infra, Stripe fees setup, staging environment, and migration tooling/licensing are included.

Total estimated hours: Backend 612h, Frontend 380h, QA 168h, DevOps 96h => base labour ~$113,058. Adding non-labour (~$9,500) gives a most-likely total of ~$122,558. P10/P50/P90 scenarios scale this by -12%/0%/+30% to reflect estimation uncertainty, especially around PW-8 (migration) and PW-7 (Stripe integration) which are historically prone to overruns.

Capacity check: Backend Developer 1.5 FTE over an assumed 16-week delivery window has ~960 hours available; allocated 612h (64%) leaves headroom for other maintenance/support, which is reasonable. Frontend 1.0 FTE over 16 weeks = 640h available; allocated 380h (59%) is reasonable. QA 0.6 FTE = 384h available; allocated 168h (44%) is reasonable, though QA is thinly staffed relative to the number of urgent features needing regression testing. DevOps 0.4 FTE = 256h available; allocated 96h (37%) is fine but tight if staging/CI issues arise during migration cutover.

scenarios.name: Optimistic (low complexity realized, no major integration issues)

nonLabourLines.description: Cloud infrastructure (staging + CI runners) for pipeline setup and ongoing builds
Stripe integration setup, sandbox testing, and webhook infra
Data migration tooling/licensing (ETL scripts, Oracle connector, validation tooling)
Design/UI asset licensing (icon sets, theming assets) for component library
Contingency buffer for third-party/API rate limits or environment provisioning delays

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available yet for this project; effort figures are based on analogy/expert judgement against similar Angular/API/Stripe/migration projects, not on this team's measured throughput.
Delivery window assumed ~16 weeks, used to sanity-check role hour allocations against available FTE capacity.
1 story point translated to roughly 6-8 hours of blended effort depending on task type (UI-heavy vs backend-heavy vs infra/migration).
QA Engineer at 0.6 FTE is thinly staffed relative to the volume of Urgent/High priority features requiring regression and security testing (auth, RBAC, payments); this is flagged as a risk.
DevOps Engineer at 0.4 FTE is concentrated on CI/staging setup (PW-1) and migration cutover support (PW-8); any additional infra incidents would require re-prioritization or a scope trim elsewhere.
Legacy data migration (PW-8) effort assumes reasonably clean source schema; actual complexity of 400k records/2M invoice lines could shift this materially, hence the wide P90 band.
Backend Developer role absorbs the largest share of hours since most backlog items (auth, RBAC, dashboard API, invoices API, Stripe integration, migration) are backend/API-centric.
Non-labour costs are rough order-of-magnitude allowances for cloud infra, Stripe setup, migration tooling, and contingency; actual vendor quotes were not available.
Priority breakdown costs are allocated proportionally to story points within each priority band using the blended hourly rate mix.

reductions.description: Descope PW-2 (Design system and component library) to a minimal set of components now, deferring full theming tokens and advanced dialog/table variants to a later phase
reductions.effect: Reduces Frontend Developer hours by ~90h; delays full design system consistency until phase 2

reductions.description: Reduce QA Engineer allocation on Medium-priority items (PW-2, PW-6) in favor of developer self-testing/peer review, reserving dedicated QA for Urgent items (auth, payments)
reductions.effect: Cuts ~50 QA hours; increases regression risk on lower-priority features

reductions.description: Defer Legacy Data Migration (PW-8) to a follow-on project phase after go-live, launching with manual/CSV import for a limited initial customer set
reductions.effect: Removes the bulk of migration-related Backend/DevOps/QA hours and tooling cost from this phase; requires an interim manual data process

reductions.description: Use a pre-built Angular UI kit (e.g. Angular Material or PrimeNG) instead of a fully custom component library for PW-2
reductions.effect: Reduces Frontend Developer build hours by ~65h at the cost of some visual customization

reductions.description: Trim non-labour contingency and migration tooling budget by negotiating a fixed-price ETL tool license instead of custom scripting
reductions.effect: Reduces non-labour spend; assumes a suitable off-the-shelf ETL tool is available for the Oracle source schema
